domain_label: Ingredient Selection, Quality & Substitution - Core Ingredient Functions & Quality (cupcake baking subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is core ingredient function and quality for cupcakes, finer than a whole-baking KB
a tested base cupcake formula exists; this KB governs ingredient choice and substitution within it
mixing method, panning, and baking are downstream and out of scope except where ingredient temperature is involved
exclusions: mixing technique, batter scaling, panning, and oven/bake profile
frosting and filling formulation beyond total-sweetness interaction
gluten-free and vegan full reformulation systems (referenced only as constraints)
regulatory labeling compliance beyond allergen identification

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLOUR_PROTEIN documents protein band and crumb match

competency_questions.question: How do you hit an intermediate protein when one flour misses?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLOUR_BLEND gives a blend ratio and effective protein

competency_questions.question: When do you use natural vs Dutch-processed cocoa?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COCOA_TYPE ties cocoa pH to leavener choice

competency_questions.question: How does chocolate %cacao change the fat and sugar in the batter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHOC_CACAO_PCT rebalances fat and sugar for the chocolate

competency_questions.question: How does butterfat and butter temperature affect crumb?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUTTERFAT and BUTTER_TEMP set richness and creaming aeration

competency_questions.question: When should oil be used instead of (or with) butter?
How do egg size, temperature, and freshness affect the batter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EGG_SIZE/EGG_TEMP/EGG_FRESH standardize liquid, emulsion, and safety

competency_questions.question: How does sugar form and crystal size affect aeration and crumb?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUGAR_FORM and SUGAR_CREAMING cover moisture and aeration roles

competency_questions.question: How do sugar forms change moisture and browning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUGAR_FORM links sugar choice to moisture and browning

competency_questions.question: How do you replace buttermilk while keeping leavening function?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUTTERMILK_SUB matches acid load for soda activation

competency_questions.question: How does cultured-dairy acidity interact with leavening?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DAIRY_ACID and SODA_ACID_BALANCE pair acid with soda

competency_questions.question: How do you confirm leavener works and balance soda to acid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAVENER_FRESH and SODA_ACID_BALANCE test and balance leavening

competency_questions.question: How are food-safety and allergen risks controlled in ingredient choice?

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALT_QUALITY and VANILLA_QUALITY tune sweetness and aroma

glossary.definition: protein network formed from flour protein and water that gives structure and chew
cocoa alkalized to neutralize acidity, darkening color and mellowing flavor
the fat fraction of butter; higher in European-style butter (~82-85%)
beating fat with sugar so crystals cut air cells into the fat for leavening
hydrolyzed sucrose (glucose+fructose) that is hygroscopic and resists crystallizing
acidic cultured dairy used for tang and to activate baking soda
sodium bicarbonate; an alkaline leavener needing an acid to release gas
a complete leavener containing soda plus dry acid, often double-acting
stable dispersion of fat and water phases that carries air and moisture in batter
reactions, pH-sensitive, that brown and flavor the crumb crust
tending to attract and hold moisture, as brown and invert sugars do
temperature range where pathogens grow, relevant to raw egg/dairy handling

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for core cupcake ingredient selection, quality, and substitution work units, informed in spirit by standard baking-science references but not quoting measured data

nodes.definition: Select flour by protein content (cake ~7-9%, pastry ~8-9%, AP ~10-12%) to set gluten potential and target crumb fineness.

included: cake vs pastry vs AP flour

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: crumb evaluation or flour supplier protein spec changes

pros.claim: Lower-protein cake flour yields a finer, more tender crumb prized in cupcakes
pros.example: cake flour at ~8% protein gives plush velvet crumb

cons.claim: Too-low protein can collapse a heavily-loaded batter lacking structure
cons.example: very wet chocolate batter sinks on cake flour alone

failure_modes: using bread flour and getting tough chewy cupcakes
acceptance_tests: protein percentage of chosen flour documented
revisit_triggers: batter structure collapses at high add-ins

nodes.definition: Blend AP with cornstarch or mix AP+cake flour to hit an intermediate protein when a single flour misses the structure/tenderness balance.

pros.claim: DIY cake-flour substitute rescues tenderness when only AP is on hand
pros.example: 1 cup AP minus 2 tbsp plus 2 tbsp cornstarch approximates cake flour

cons.claim: Cornstarch dilution lowers structure and can dull flavor if overdone
cons.example: over-substituting yields gummy centers

failure_modes: ignoring that cornstarch has no gluten
revisit_triggers: substitute crumb differs from true cake flour

nodes.definition: Choose natural vs Dutch-processed cocoa by required acidity and color, because cocoa pH drives both flavor and leavener pairing.

pros.claim: Matching cocoa pH to the leavener prevents flat or metallic cupcakes
pros.example: natural cocoa with baking soda gives reliable lift and reddish hue

cons.claim: Swapping Dutch for natural without adjusting leavener breaks the acid-base balance
cons.example: Dutch cocoa with only soda underleavens and tastes soapy

failure_modes: pairing Dutch cocoa with soda-only leavening
revisit_triggers: color off target after cocoa swap

nodes.definition: Select melted-chocolate %cacao to balance added fat, sugar, and chocolate intensity contributed to the batter.

pros.claim: Higher %cacao deepens flavor but adds cocoa butter that enriches crumb
pros.example: 70% chocolate adds fat that softens the crumb

cons.claim: Swapping chocolates of different %cacao shifts fat and sugar unaccounted
cons.example: unsweetened to bittersweet swap oversweetens batter

failure_modes: ignoring sugar already in the chocolate
acceptance_tests: fat and sugar rebalanced for chosen chocolate
revisit_triggers: batter too greasy or too sweet after chocolate change

nodes.definition: Choose butter by butterfat and water content (standard ~80% vs European-style ~82-85%) to control richness, moisture, and creaming behavior.

pros.claim: Higher-butterfat European butter enriches flavor and crumb tenderness
pros.example: 82%+ butter yields plusher, more flavorful cupcakes

cons.claim: Lower water in high-fat butter changes hydration and can reduce steam lift
cons.example: substituting European butter without adjusting liquid dries crumb

failure_modes: ignoring water content shift on butter swap
acceptance_tests: liquid adjusted for butter water content
revisit_triggers: crumb drier or denser after butter swap

nodes.definition: Bring butter to proper creaming temperature (~65-67F) so it aerates and traps air cells that seed the crumb structure.

pros.claim: Correctly tempered butter creams to a light aerated base giving fine even crumb
pros.example: 65F butter whips to pale fluffy mass holding air

cons.claim: Too-warm butter cannot hold air and yields dense greasy cupcakes
cons.example: melted-edge butter collapses the foam

acceptance_tests: butter temperature in range before creaming

nodes.definition: Decide oil vs butter (or a blend) trading butter's flavor and creaming aeration against oil's persistent moistness and shelf-life.

pros.claim: Oil stays liquid at room temp keeping cupcakes moist for days
pros.example: oil-based cupcakes resist staling longer than all-butter

cons.claim: Oil contributes no flavor and cannot cream to aerate, risking dense flat tops
cons.example: all-oil vanilla cupcakes taste flat and rise less

failure_modes: relying on oil for aeration that needs creaming
acceptance_tests: fat strategy chosen against flavor/moisture priority
leavening compensates for lost creaming if oil used
revisit_triggers: cupcakes stale fast or taste flat

nodes.definition: Standardize egg size by weight (large ~50g) so the batter's liquid, protein, and emulsifier load stay consistent batch to batch.

pros.claim: Weighing eggs removes size variance that shifts hydration and structure
pros.example: two jumbo eggs over-wet a recipe written for large

cons.claim: Weighing adds a step many home bakers skip
cons.example: scale-free bakers accept size drift

acceptance_tests: eggs measured by weight or size specified
liquid load consistent batch to batch

nodes.definition: Use room-temperature eggs so the butter-sugar emulsion does not break and the batter incorporates air smoothly.

pros.claim: Room-temp eggs blend into the creamed base without breaking the emulsion
pros.example: 65F eggs fold in smoothly keeping the foam intact

cons.claim: Cold eggs shock the fat and curdle the batter, losing trapped air
cons.example: fridge-cold eggs seize the butter into specks

failure_modes: adding cold eggs to creamed butter
acceptance_tests: eggs at room temperature before mixing

nodes.definition: Assess egg freshness and handle raw egg for food safety, since freshness affects foaming and raw-egg use carries salmonella risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: egg source or unbaked-component plan changes

pros.claim: Fresh eggs whip higher and signal safe handling for the bake
pros.example: fresh whites foam to greater volume for light crumb

cons.claim: Raw or undercooked egg in batter risks salmonella and must be controlled
cons.example: tasting raw batter exposes consumers to pathogens

failure_modes: using spoiled eggs in unbaked components
acceptance_tests: raw-egg exposure avoided or pasteurized eggs used

nodes.definition: Select sugar form (granulated, brown, invert/honey) for sweetness, moisture retention, and browning behavior in the crumb.

pros.claim: Brown sugar's molasses adds moisture and deeper flavor and aids browning
pros.example: brown sugar cupcakes stay moister and taste richer

cons.claim: Swapping sugar forms changes acidity, moisture, and sweetness all at once
cons.example: brown for white shifts pH and can over-brown

failure_modes: ignoring brown sugar acidity effect on leavening

nodes.definition: Use granulated sugar's crystal edges during creaming to mechanically cut air pockets into the fat, leveraging sugar as an aerating tool.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sweetener form change in creaming step

pros.claim: Granulated crystals create air cells during creaming for an even rise
pros.example: standard sugar aerates butter better than powdered

cons.claim: Liquid or very fine sweeteners cannot mechanically aerate the fat
cons.example: honey-only batter loses the creaming lift

failure_modes: using powdered sugar where aeration is needed
acceptance_tests: granulated sugar used where aeration required

nodes.definition: Use buttermilk or sour cream both for tang and as the acid that activates baking soda and tenderizes by weakening gluten.

pros.claim: Buttermilk supplies acid to react soda and tenderizes for a soft tangy crumb
pros.example: buttermilk + soda gives lift, tang, and tender texture

cons.claim: Removing cultured dairy strands the soda unreacted, dulling lift and flavor
cons.example: swapping buttermilk for milk leaves soapy soda taste

failure_modes: dropping the acid source but keeping soda
ignoring fat difference of sour cream vs buttermilk
acceptance_tests: acid source quantified for soda activation

nodes.definition: Construct a buttermilk substitute (milk + acid) when needed, matching acid load so soda activation and tenderizing are preserved.

pros.claim: Milk plus a measured acid replaces buttermilk's leavening function
pros.example: 1 tbsp lemon per cup milk approximates buttermilk acidity

cons.claim: Substitute lacks the cultured flavor depth of real buttermilk
cons.example: tang is thinner than true buttermilk

revisit_triggers: lift or tang weaker than with real buttermilk

nodes.definition: Test baking soda and baking powder freshness before use, because stale leavener silently kills rise regardless of recipe correctness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: leavener age or storage condition changes

pros.claim: A quick fizz test catches dead leavener before wasting a whole batch
pros.example: baking powder bubbling in hot water confirms it is active

cons.claim: Skipping the test risks flat dense cupcakes from inert leavener
cons.example: expired powder yields no rise and dense crumb

nodes.definition: Balance baking soda against the batter's total acid (cocoa, brown sugar, cultured dairy) to drive lift and pH-dependent browning without soapy off-notes.

pros.claim: Right soda:acid gives full lift and warm browning without metallic taste
pros.example: balanced soda neutralizes acid and tints crumb darker

cons.claim: Excess soda leaves a soapy alkaline taste and coarse crumb
cons.example: too much soda tastes metallic and over-browns

failure_modes: ignoring acid from cocoa and brown sugar
acceptance_tests: soda balanced to total acid inventory
no soapy taste in baked sample

nodes.definition: Choose salt type and dose by weight to enhance flavor and modulate sweetness perception, accounting for crystal-size volume differences.

included: table vs kosher vs fine sea salt

pros.claim: Salt sharpens chocolate and vanilla and tempers cloying sweetness
pros.example: a pinch of salt makes the cupcake taste less flatly sweet

cons.claim: Measuring coarse salt by volume over- or under-doses versus fine salt
cons.example: kosher-for-table swap by volume under-salts

failure_modes: volume-swapping salts of different crystal size
acceptance_tests: flavor balanced not flat or harsh

nodes.definition: Select vanilla form (extract, paste, bean) and quality, and add at the right stage so heat-sensitive aroma survives into the crumb.

pros.claim: Pure vanilla adds rounded aromatic complexity that imitation cannot match
pros.example: real vanilla bean specks signal and deliver deeper aroma

cons.claim: High-quality vanilla is costly and easy to over- or under-dose
cons.example: over-extracting masks delicate batter flavors

failure_modes: losing aroma to excessive heat exposure

nodes.definition: Coordinate all wet ingredients to a common (room) temperature so the batter forms one stable emulsion rather than separating.

pros.claim: Matched temperatures let fat, egg, and dairy emulsify into a uniform batter
pros.example: all-room-temp ingredients fold into a glossy stable batter

cons.claim: Mixing cold dairy into warm fat breaks the emulsion and traps less air
cons.example: cold buttermilk seizes the creamed base

failure_modes: one cold ingredient breaking the emulsion
over-warming risking safety or melting fat
acceptance_tests: wet ingredients within a common temperature band

nodes.definition: Balance total moisture-contributing ingredients (oil, sugar, dairy, eggs) against structure-builders (flour protein, eggs) for a moist yet stable cupcake that domes and holds.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any moisture or structure ingredient changes

pros.claim: Balanced moisture and structure yields a moist crumb that still domes and holds shape
pros.example: right liquid:flour gives tender yet standing cupcakes

cons.claim: Pushing moisture too far collapses structure into a gummy sunken center
cons.example: over-wet batter sinks and tunnels

failure_modes: over-structured batter baking dry and tough
acceptance_tests: baked cupcakes domed and not gummy

nodes.definition: Identify and control common allergens (wheat/gluten, egg, dairy, nuts in flavorings) across ingredient selection and substitution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ingredient substitution or audience allergy change

pros.claim: Documented allergens protect consumers and guide safe substitutions
pros.example: disclosing wheat/egg/dairy lets allergic guests avoid harm

cons.claim: Ingredient swaps can silently introduce or hide allergens
cons.example: a nut-derived flavoring added without disclosure endangers guests

acceptance_tests: allergen inventory complete for the formula

edges.risk_of_conflict: blend drifts from target if base choice unset

edges.why_related: chocolate fat/sugar choices follow the cocoa acidity decision
creaming temperature depends on the butter's fat/water
the oil/butter decision builds on butter properties
edges.risk_of_conflict: flavor lost if butter role unset
edges.example: butter+oil blend for flavor and moisture

edges.why_related: eggs are tempered to match the creamed butter base
edges.risk_of_conflict: curdling if egg cold after creaming

edges.why_related: sugar aerates the fat at creaming temperature
edges.benefit_of_coupling: crystals cut air into soft butter

edges.why_related: creaming aeration depends on sugar crystal form
substitute must reproduce the acid role of cultured dairy
edges.risk_of_conflict: unreacted soda if acid not matched

edges.why_related: cocoa pH is a major acid input to the soda balance
edges.example: natural cocoa adds acid for soda

edges.why_related: cultured dairy acid feeds the soda balance
brown sugar acidity shifts the soda balance
edges.example: brown sugar adds acid to balance

edges.why_related: balance assumes the leavener is actually active
edges.example: test soda before relying on it

edges.why_related: butter temperature is part of overall temperature coordination
edges.risk_of_conflict: emulsion breaks if one is cold
edges.example: stage all wets to room temp

edges.why_related: egg temperature feeds overall coordination
dairy temperature is coordinated with the batter
flour protein sets the structure side of the moisture balance
edges.example: cake flour limits liquid it can hold

edges.why_related: fat strategy is a major moisture input to the balance
sugar form contributes moisture to the balance
cultured dairy adds liquid and tenderizing to the balance
edges.example: sour cream adds fat and moisture

edges.why_related: egg quantity adds both liquid and structure to the balance
cocoa solids dilute flour structure constraining protein choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak structure if cocoa load ignored

edges.why_related: freshness and safety constrain how eggs are warmed and used
edges.risk_of_conflict: spoilage risk if warmed too long

edges.why_related: both are flavor enhancers tuned to round out sweetness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: salt and vanilla jointly balance flavor

edges.why_related: leavening pH and rise interact with moisture and structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: sinking if lift fails wet batter
edges.example: good lift holds a moist crumb

edges.why_related: egg is both a safety and an allergen concern
edges.benefit_of_coupling: egg handled for safety and allergy
edges.example: egg flagged as allergen and hazard

edges.why_related: wheat flour is the primary gluten allergen to control
edges.example: wheat flour flagged for celiac guests

edges.why_related: dairy ingredients are a controlled allergen
oil's moistness competes with butter's creaming aeration
edges.example: oil moist but flat vs butter aerated
edges.resolution_rule: when doming and flavor are required butter-creaming dominates; use oil only with added chemical leavening and accept less aeration

edges.why_related: more moisture for tenderness fights the structure flour provides
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tune both to a stable point
edges.example: wet tender batter vs standing crumb
edges.resolution_rule: structural integrity dominates: cap added moisture at the liquid:flour the chosen protein can hold; raise protein before adding liquid

edges.why_related: sweetness/moisture from more sugar shifts acidity and browning
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balance soda to the sugar acidity
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-browning or off lift if unmanaged
edges.resolution_rule: flavor-correctness dominates: re-balance soda to the sugar's acid load rather than leaving excess soda, even if it caps how much brown sugar is used

edges.why_related: flavor complexity from more flavorings competes with batter water balance
edges.risk_of_conflict: liquid extracts add to moisture load
edges.resolution_rule: moisture balance dominates: deliver added flavor via paste/bean or reduce other liquid so total hydration stays in band

edges.why_related: sour cream's fat richness competes with buttermilk's leaner tang at fixed fat budget
edges.benefit_of_coupling: pick the dairy matching fat target
edges.risk_of_conflict: fat budget overshoot if both added
edges.example: sour cream rich vs buttermilk tangy
edges.resolution_rule: fat-budget balance dominates: choose one cultured dairy to hit the richness target and adjust butter accordingly rather than stacking both

edges.why_related: higher %cacao adds cocoa butter that enriches but loads the fat/moisture balance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: account chocolate fat in the balance
edges.risk_of_conflict: greasy crumb if chocolate fat ignored
edges.resolution_rule: moisture/fat balance dominates: subtract added cocoa-butter fat from other fats when raising %cacao

edges.why_related: the most delicious flour blend may conflict with an allergen-free requirement
edges.risk_of_conflict: allergic harm if taste overrides safety
edges.example: best crumb flour vs gluten-free need
edges.resolution_rule: food safety dominates: allergen-free requirement overrides the preferred flour blend; reformulate to a safe equivalent

edges.why_related: raw-egg richness/tasting tempts but raw-egg safety overrides texture goals
edges.benefit_of_coupling: favor safe handling over raw richness
edges.risk_of_conflict: pathogen risk if raw egg tasted/served
edges.resolution_rule: food safety dominates: never rely on raw egg in served/unbaked components; use pasteurized egg or bake fully regardless of texture appeal

edges.why_related: butter water content changes the moisture the balance must account
edges.risk_of_conflict: dry crumb if water shift ignored

edges.why_related: aeration from creaming affects crumb openness and perceived moistness
salt level changes perceived sweetness from the chosen sugar
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tune salt to the sugar sweetness

edges.why_related: vanilla and chocolate intensity are jointly tuned flavor levers
a stable emulsion holds moisture in the crumb better
edges.risk_of_conflict: broken batter leaks fat and dries

conflict_axes.trigger: adding liquid/oil/sugar for moistness weakens the crumb until it sinks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if centers sink or crumb is gummy, structural integrity dominates and moisture is capped
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sunken center or gummy core observed
conflict_axes.example: very wet chocolate batter on cake flour collapses

conflict_axes.trigger: tenderizing (low protein, oil, less mixing) reduces the structure that lets tops dome
resolution_order: choose protein for minimum needed structure
add chemical leavening to recover rise
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if doming is a product requirement, rise/structure side dominates over maximal tenderness

conflict_axes.trigger: raising sugar for sweetness flattens and masks aromatic complexity
resolution_order: use salt and vanilla to add complexity
reduce sugar if flavor reads flat
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: when flavor reads flat, complexity side dominates and sugar is trimmed toward the functional minimum
conflict_axes.example: over-sugared vanilla cupcake tastes flatly sweet

conflict_axes.trigger: a sweet frosting plus a sweet cake stacks into cloying total sweetness
resolution_order: reduce cake sugar when frosting is sweet
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: total assembled sweetness dominates: trim cake sugar so the finished cupcake is balanced
conflict_axes.example: sweet buttercream over sweet cake overwhelms

conflict_axes.trigger: shortcuts (substitutes, cold ingredients, skipping tests) save time but lower quality
resolution_order: identify which step the shortcut touches
verify function (acid load, protein, aeration) preserved
accept shortcut only if function holds
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for quality-critical functions, quality dominates; substitutes allowed only when they reproduce the function
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: quality drop traced to a shortcut

conflict_axes.trigger: butter gives best-fresh flavor/texture but firms and stales faster than oil
resolution_order: use oil or oil/butter blend for hold
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if cupcakes must hold for days, shelf-life side favors oil; for serve-fresh, butter texture dominates
conflict_axes.example: all-butter cupcakes dry by day two

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing cocoa for color/flavor changes batter pH and the leavener it needs
resolution_order: verify lift and no soapy taste
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: leavening balance dominates: cocoa choice must be paired with a matching soda:acid plan
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: soapy taste or flat chocolate cupcakes

conflict_axes.trigger: stacking high-fat butter, high %cacao, and sour cream overshoots the fat budget and greases the crumb
resolution_order: hold total fat in the moisture/structure band
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: moisture/fat balance dominates: cap total fat by trading sources rather than stacking them
conflict_axes.example: European butter + 70% chocolate + sour cream greases batter

conflict_axes.trigger: appealing raw-egg richness or a tastier allergen-containing formula conflicts with safety
resolution_order: identify any raw-egg or allergen exposure
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: food safety is a hard override: raw-egg/allergen/temperature-danger concerns dominate all flavor and texture goals
conflict_axes.example: raw batter tasting or undisclosed nut flavoring is blocked

edge_cases.trigger: Dutch cocoa used with soda-only leavening
edge_cases.failure_mode: alkaline batter underleavens and tastes soapy
edge_cases.example: swap to Dutch without leavener change
edge_cases.detection_method: check cocoa pH against leavener plan
resolution: add baking powder or an acid

edge_cases.failure_mode: no rise, dense crumb despite correct recipe
edge_cases.example: old baking powder gives no fizz

edge_cases.trigger: cold eggs added to creamed butter
edge_cases.failure_mode: emulsion curdles and loses trapped air

edge_cases.trigger: raw-egg batter tasted or served unbaked
bread flour used in place of cake/AP
excess baking soda beyond available acid
edge_cases.failure_mode: soapy metallic taste and coarse crumb
edge_cases.example: too much soda for the acid present
edge_cases.detection_method: compute soda:acid against all acid sources

edge_cases.trigger: all-oil batter relied on for aeration
edge_cases.failure_mode: flat dense tops, no creaming lift
edge_cases.example: oil recipe with no chemical leavening boost
edge_cases.detection_method: check leavening when fat is liquid

edge_cases.trigger: European butter swapped for standard without liquid adjustment
edge_cases.failure_mode: drier denser crumb from lower water
edge_cases.detection_method: track butter water content in hydration

edge_cases.trigger: buttermilk replaced by plain milk, soda kept
edge_cases.failure_mode: unreacted soda, weak rise, soapy note
edge_cases.example: acid source dropped but soda kept
edge_cases.detection_method: verify acid present for every soda use

edge_cases.trigger: coarse salt measured by volume as if fine
edge_cases.failure_mode: under- or over-salting and flavor imbalance
edge_cases.example: kosher salt used in a table-salt recipe by volume

edge_cases.detection_method: check all wets at common temperature
resolution: bring all wets to room temp

workflow.do_first_because: all structure and moisture decisions build on the flour protein

workflow.objective: choose butter grade, temperature, and oil/butter balance
workflow.do_first_because: fat choice drives flavor, aeration, moisture, and shelf-life

acceptance_tests: cocoa pH paired with leavener plan
workflow.do_first_because: cocoa pH must be settled before the leavening balance

workflow.objective: select sugar forms and confirm creaming aeration role
workflow.do_first_because: sugar form sets sweetness, moisture, browning, and aeration

workflow.do_first_because: egg size, temperature, and safety underpin emulsion and food safety

workflow.objective: choose cultured dairy or a matched substitute for acid and tang
workflow.do_first_because: cultured dairy acid feeds the leavening balance and tenderness

workflow.objective: test leavener and balance soda against total acid
workflow.do_first_because: leavening must be balanced and active or the cupcake fails to rise

workflow.objective: dose salt and select vanilla to balance and complete flavor
workflow.do_first_because: salt and vanilla tune sweetness perception and aroma

workflow.objective: coordinate ingredient temperatures for a stable emulsion
workflow.do_first_because: a stable emulsion is required before final balance

workflow.objective: balance moisture against structure for a moist, standing crumb
workflow.do_first_because: the moisture/structure balance integrates every prior choice

workflow.objective: final allergen and food-safety review across the formula
workflow.do_first_because: food safety must clear before any cupcake is served

dominance_rules.trigger: raw-egg or undercooked egg/dairy exposure in a served component
dominance_rules.rule: food safety overrides flavor and texture; no raw-egg reliance in served/unbaked components
dominance_rules.required_action: use pasteurized egg or bake fully
dominance_rules.example: raw batter tasting is disallowed regardless of appeal

dominance_rules.trigger: an undisclosed allergen would improve taste
dominance_rules.rule: allergen control overrides flavor; disclose or remove and reformulate safely
dominance_rules.example: a tastier nut flavoring is removed if guests are nut-allergic

dominance_rules.trigger: ingredients held in the temperature danger zone too long
dominance_rules.rule: temperature safety overrides convenience when warming ingredients
dominance_rules.required_action: limit warming time; chill if exceeded
dominance_rules.example: do not leave egg/dairy out beyond safe time to temper

dominance_rules.trigger: added moisture would sink the crumb
dominance_rules.rule: structure dominates once centers sink; cap moisture to protein capacity
dominance_rules.example: trim liquid when chocolate cupcakes sink

dominance_rules.trigger: cocoa/sugar choice conflicts with leavening balance
dominance_rules.rule: soda:acid balance dominates cocoa/sugar aesthetic choices
dominance_rules.required_action: pair cocoa choice with matching leavener plan
dominance_rules.example: Dutch cocoa requires added acid or powder

dominance_rules.rule: verified-active leavener dominates; do not bake on untested old leavener
finished-cupcake balance dominates individual component sweetness
dominance_rules.required_action: trim cake sugar when frosting is sweet
dominance_rules.example: reduce cake sugar under sweet buttercream

dominance_rules.rule: total fat budget dominates stacking of rich ingredients
dominance_rules.required_action: trade fat sources instead of adding all
dominance_rules.example: cap total fat across butter, chocolate, sour cream

dominance_rules.trigger: a shortcut would drop a quality-critical function
dominance_rules.rule: preserved function dominates convenience; substitutes only if function holds
dominance_rules.example: buttermilk substitute must match acid load

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix flour protein before tuning moisture or add-ins
anti_rework_rules.rationale: structure capacity bounds how much moisture the crumb can carry

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle cocoa process before balancing leavening
anti_rework_rules.rationale: cocoa pH is a primary acid input to the soda balance

anti_rework_rules.rule: quantify all acid sources before setting baking soda
anti_rework_rules.rationale: soda must match total acid or leaves soapy excess
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: soda set before acid inventory complete
anti_rework_rules.example: dosing soda before counting buttermilk/brown sugar

anti_rework_rules.rule: test leavener freshness before relying on the recipe
anti_rework_rules.rationale: stale leavener silently fails any balance

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose butter grade before setting creaming and hydration
anti_rework_rules.rationale: butter water and fat change aeration and hydration
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hydration set before butter grade known

anti_rework_rules.rule: standardize egg size/weight before fixing batter hydration
anti_rework_rules.rationale: egg size variance shifts liquid and structure
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hydration locked before egg size set

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete allergen screen before finalizing any substitution
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: finalizing a swap without allergen check

anti_rework_rules.rule: control raw-egg safety before any tasting or unbaked use
anti_rework_rules.rationale: raw egg carries pathogen risk that overrides texture

anti_rework_rules.rule: stabilize the emulsion before judging the moisture balance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a broken emulsion leaks fat and misreads moisture
anti_rework_rules.example: mixing cold dairy into warm fat

iteration_protocol.trigger: baked sample tastes soapy or metallic

iteration_protocol.detection: bake observation of dense flat cupcakes

test_cases.input_summary: vanilla cupcake, AP flour, butter, large eggs
natural cocoa swapped to Dutch without leavener change
extra oil and sugar added for moistness

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked artifact change
increment on leavening or moisture balance change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade soft_lock to draft on upstream dependency change
